title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover hysteresis
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: During a regional capacity incident we observed SLO enforcer backoff oscillations that caused repeated regional failover and load-shedding cycles. This led to transient high error rates and degraded availability for Dedicated customers. Root cause: the backoff/hysteresis logic in the SLO enforcer did not account for out-of-order state transitions when regional health signals arrived concurrently, and the smoothing window used for failure rate estimation was too short under bursty load.

This PR: 1) fixes ordering and atomicity in the SLO enforcer's state machine when applying backoff and regional-failover decisions (use compare-and-swap and single-threaded decision executor per region); 2) increases the smoothing window and switches to an exponentially-weighted moving average for failure-rate estimation to reduce sensitivity to brief spikes; 3) adds a minimum hysteresis period to prevent immediate re-enabling of a region after a failover; 4) introduces feature-flag guarded rollout (sre.slo_enforcer.stable_backoff) and a config knob for hysteresis_ms; 5) adds unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent health signals and bursty loads; 6) small telemetry/metrics changes: new metrics slo_enforcer.backoff_state_transitions and slo_enforcer.hysteresis_skips for monitoring regressions.

Testing and rollout notes: CI: unit + integration + e2e smoke all pass after two re-runs. Staged rollout to production via the canary policy in Redwood Console (10% -> 50% -> 100%) gated by the new backoff_state_transitions alert. Feature flag default is OFF; SRE will enable for the affected regions after canary validation.

Related: ENG-3421 (investigation), SUP-903 (customer incident), several prior hotfixes for SLO enforcer hysteresis in the past year.
